passage: Most modern maps place north at the top. This convention is so familiar that many people assume it is the natural way to draw the world. But early maps from several cultures placed east, south, or even a sacred site at the top, depending on what the mapmakers considered most important.
stem: Which choice best describes the function of the third sentence in the overall structure of the text?
choices: It challenges the assumption described in the second sentence by giving counterexamples.
It explains why mapmakers eventually agreed to place north at the top of their maps.
It provides an example that supports the assumption described in the second sentence.
It introduces a new topic about how ancient mapmakers measured distances and directions.
steps: Sentence 2: many assume north-at-top is natural.
Sentence 3 begins with "But" and lists maps with other directions on top.
Those examples show the assumption is wrong, so they are counterexamples.
It doesn't explain agreement, support the assumption, or discuss measurement.
key: A sentence starting with "But" after an assumption usually challenges it.
